status: E0 synthetic decision fixtures; every numerical value is invented for testing contract behavior and is not measured hardware data
thesis: A successor counts as better only on a declared, evidence-qualified objective while preserving every hard-required predecessor capability. There is no universal scalar successor score. Replication, exact design correctness, measured workload improvement, local manufacture, and semiconductor fab closure are distinct claims.

target_path.name: Conventional compute baseline
target_path.evidence_claim: Frozen software workload and reference output only.

target_path.name: Reproduction-capable cell
target_path.evidence_claim: C4/C5 only when physical host-assisted and host-removal tests have witnessed receipts; C5 alone does not prove more compute performance.

target_path.name: Better testing / repair / tooling
target_path.evidence_claim: Specific new inspection, programming, repair or calibration route demonstrated under a declared profile.

target_path.name: Exact HDC RTL accelerator
target_path.evidence_claim: Reference/RTL exact semantic agreement and admitted formal-property evidence; no performance claim from simulation alone.

target_path.name: FPGA-observed accelerator
target_path.evidence_claim: Target implementation and physical board observed; end-to-end measured gain compared with the frozen conventional baseline.

target_path.name: External ASIC design/submission
target_path.evidence_claim: Version-pinned physical design and submission receipts; still not fabricated silicon.

target_path.name: Packaged/tested successor
target_path.evidence_claim: Fabrication receipt, package/test records and system integration evidence; fabrication remains external unless separate evidence establishes local fab closure.

hard_requirements: All protected predecessor capabilities remain available under the successor profile, or any trade-off is explicitly declared and not promoted as an unconditional improvement.
Exact operations must match the frozen BinaryHV software oracle unless a separate approximation profile is versioned and task-level behavior is evaluated.
Performance comparisons use the same pinned workload/input and include host/device transfer, preprocessing, batching and output conversion when those are part of deployment.
A metric may be used only if its evidence tier supports the claim; simulation, synthesis estimates, FPGA board measurements and packaged-device measurements are distinct.
Unknown, stale or conflicting evidence remains unresolved and cannot be imputed as true.
Independent dimensions remain separate; do not collapse throughput, latency, energy, accuracy, robustness, repairability, import dependence or tool renewal into one weighted score.

proposed_first_hdc_win_gate.label: proposed; freeze before physical candidate measurements
proposed_first_hdc_win_gate.correctness: zero unexplained mismatches on every preregistered exact HDC fixture
proposed_first_hdc_win_gate.measurable_alternative: at least 2x end-to-end throughput OR at least 30% lower measured system energy for the same declared workload and equivalent output
guardrails: No protected latency, thermal, area/resource, correctness or task-utility constraint is violated.
Include device transfer, setup, batching and host-side overhead in end-to-end metrics.
Measure system energy at the same explicit boundary; FPGA tool power estimates alone do not qualify as measured system energy.
If neither alternative gate is met, report no demonstrated advantage; do not tune metrics after observing candidate results.

claim_rules: C5 reproduction is a useful capability gain but not a compute-performance improvement.
RTL equivalence is a correctness gate, not an accelerator advantage.
FPGA synthesis/resource reports are not physical power or speed measurements.
GDS generation or external MPW submission is not proof that a die was fabricated.
Externally fabricated and packaged silicon is not locally closed semiconductor manufacturing.
An extra capability does not compensate automatically for regression of a hard-required capability.

fixtures.intent: Distinguish reproduction capability from successor capability gain.

expected.reason: The cell can reproduce a computer, but no computing/workload metric improved.

fixtures.intent: A new, qualified test fixture improves product acceptance capability without claiming faster compute.

expected.reason: Testing/reproducibility improved; no compute-performance claim follows.

fixtures.intent: Exact HDC RTL is qualified for semantics but no hardware performance result exists.

expected.reason: Equivalence is necessary but is not physical FPGA observation or measured system advantage.

fixtures.intent: Negative control for an accelerator whose data transfer/setup dominates.

expected.reason: Kernel throughput improves but the end-to-end deployed workload regresses throughput, latency and energy.

fixtures.intent: Synthetic positive control for the proposed win gate; numbers are not empirical.

expected.reason: The synthetic candidate reaches the ≥2x throughput gate and reduces energy while preserving exact output and hard constraints; physical result required in reality.

fixtures.intent: A large throughput gain must not mask a protected tail-latency regression.

expected.reason: Throughput gain violates the protected latency profile.

fixtures.intent: Synthesis timing/resources or estimated power cannot satisfy measured system-energy gate.

expected.reason: No physical FPGA observation or system-level measurement exists.

fixtures.intent: Separate external physical design/submission capability from fabricated hardware.

expected.reason: A GDS/layout and shuttle submission do not prove a die was fabricated, packaged, tested or integrated.

fixtures.intent: Recognize actual external silicon evidence while keeping local-fab closure separate.

expected.reason: Hardware existence/qualification is distinct from local manufacturing independence and from workload performance advantage.

fixtures.intent: A stale required measurement reference must leave the successor acceptance unresolved.

expected.reason: Physical assembly may occur, but the required test capability cannot be qualified with stale calibration evidence.

fixtures.intent: A successor must not silently lose a protected predecessor function.

expected.reason: The accelerator gain does not compensate for loss of protected offline recovery.

fixtures.intent: Unknown inventory or toolchain state is unresolved, not a successful import-independent capability.

expected.reason: Missing evidence about required tools and programming interfaces blocks successor qualification.

fixtures.intent: A reproducible software/RTL build advances evidence quality but not physical hardware claims.

expected.reason: Reproducible source/artifacts do not imply FPGA observation, silicon fabrication, or performance improvement.

invariants: Candidate and baseline must use the same workload identity, source/input fixtures and declared measurement boundary for any performance comparison.
A clone/copy count increase is not a compute-performance delta.
Exact HDC algebra and any approximate mapping are different profiles; no silent conversion.
A candidate with unresolved required evidence cannot be promoted.
A protected predecessor capability loss rejects unconditional promotion even if another metric improves.
A measured performance win requires end-to-end device/host costs and equivalent task output.
Physical FPGA result, external foundry submission, fabricated die, package test, and local die-fabrication closure are different evidence claims.
No scalar weighted successor score; expose independent metrics and Pareto/conditional-Pareto status through canonical CIV-BOOT-004 semantics.
Capability-envelope comparisons reuse CIV-BOOT-003 semantics; this corpus does not define a second envelope engine.
All current fixtures are synthetic E0 checks; none is real accelerator or manufacturing evidence.

benchmark_methodology.status: design guidance derived from external references; not Symthaea result data

comparison_tracks.acceptance: bit-identical output against the pinned canonical BinaryHV software oracle for every required fixture
comparison_tracks.permitted_claim: exact semantic equivalence at the tested profile only
comparison_tracks.disallowed_inference: no automatic inference of speed, lower energy, FPGA operation, or ASIC qualification

comparison_tracks.acceptance: representation/version frozen; preregistered task-quality floor and robustness criteria; device variation, drift/noise, calibration age and repeatability measured
comparison_tracks.permitted_claim: only task-level and hardware properties directly measured for this representation/profile
comparison_tracks.disallowed_inference: must not inherit an exact-digital PASS; never silently mix with exact BinaryHV results

preregistration.current_project_hypothesis: at least 2x end-to-end throughput OR at least 30% lower measured system energy, with equivalent output and every protected hard constraint preserved
preregistration.threshold_note: project-specific hypothesis only; not an MLPerf rule or universal scientific standard

measurement_boundaries.policy: energy or latency values from different measurement boundaries are not directly comparable; only the preregistered end-to-end boundary may satisfy the system-advantage gate

benchmark_methodology.synthetic_fixture_policy: All 13 RAT fixtures remain invented examples for contract testing. External published numbers are source context only and must never be treated as Symthaea measurements.
